route.name: Traditional
route.whatItIs: The client's design team completes the design; contractors then price and build it. The client keeps design control.
route.bestWhen: Design can be completed before tender; cost certainty and design quality matter more than speed.
route.watchOuts: Slowest route to site. Gaps in the design become client variations. Little contractor input to buildability.

model.name: Lump sum
model.whatItIs: One agreed price for a defined scope; the contractor carries the risk of its own pricing.
model.bestWhen: Scope and design are well defined and the client wants a firm price at award.
model.watchOuts: Unclear or changing scope leads to variations and claims. Contractors add risk allowances where information is poor.

contract.jct: JCT Intermediate (IC); ICD where the contractor designs part (e.g. M&E)
contract.nec4: ECC Option A (priced contract with activity schedule); ECSC for simple low-value work
contract.notes: Tender on a full specification or bills of quantities.

routeToMarket.name: Framework — direct award
routeToMarket.whatItIs: Direct appointment of one framework contractor, where the framework rules allow.
routeToMarket.bestWhen: Speed is critical, or early engagement with a proven contractor is needed (often with two-stage).
routeToMarket.watchOuts: Public and eligible bodies only. Less price competition — needs a strong cost consultant. Must follow the framework's award rules.

route.name: Two-stage (PCSA)
route.whatItIs: A contractor is appointed early under a pre-construction services agreement on fees and prelims, helps develop the design, then prices the works open-book for the second stage.
route.bestWhen: Complex, occupied or phased work, or poor existing information, where early contractor input to sequencing and buildability pays off.
route.watchOuts: Less price competition at the second stage. Needs a strong cost consultant to test the price. Scope creep if not controlled.

model.name: Lump sum
model.whatItIs: One agreed price for a defined scope; the contractor carries the risk of its own pricing.
model.bestWhen: Scope and design are well defined and the client wants a firm price at award.
model.watchOuts: Unclear or changing scope leads to variations and claims. Contractors add risk allowances where information is poor.

contract.jct: JCT Pre-Construction Services Agreement (PCSA), then JCT DB (or SBC)
contract.nec4: First stage under NEC4 Professional Service Contract (PSC); construction under ECC Option A
contract.notes: Test the second-stage price against benchmarks before signing.

routeToMarket.name: Selective tender
routeToMarket.whatItIs: A shortlist of 4–6 suitable contractors is invited to tender.
routeToMarket.bestWhen: The client wants competition among contractors of proven capability.
routeToMarket.watchOuts: Public bodies above the threshold need a compliant procedure (e.g. competitive flexible) to shortlist. Prequalification takes time.

aiProse.executiveSummary: This feasibility study examines the refurbishment of Hargreaves Teaching Block, a three-storey 1960s education building at Example University, Birmingham (1200 m² GIFA). The project will replace life-expired mechanical, electrical and plumbing services, upgrade fire safety, improve thermal performance, and deliver modern flexible teaching space to support the university's net-zero plan. The estimated project cost is £2,213,000 to £2,708,000 (excluding VAT), with Grade A confidence. The target date of 1 September 2028 is achievable. The principal risk is asbestos removal and the constraint of vacation-only working.
keyFindings: The works cost mid-point is £1,507,000 (range £1,356,000–£1,658,000), driven by full systems replacement, asbestos removal, and complex mechanical and electrical installations across the entire building.
The target date of 1 September 2028 is achievable from a start of 11 January 2027, with a programme buffer of approximately 9 weeks.
The stated budget of £4,500,000 (including fees and VAT) is sufficient against the estimated gross range, with headroom of approximately £1,250,000 above the top of the range.
Asbestos is known or suspected in the building; a refurbishment and demolition survey must be commissioned before Stage 2 design to confirm scope and cost.
The preferred procurement option is Traditional with Lump sum, which offers design control and cost certainty, favoured by the client's priority for fixed final cost.
scopeAssumptions: External plant space for the air source heat pump is included within the scope and cost estimate.

The scope includes full replacement of heating, ventilation, electrical, water, drainage and data systems across the entire 1200 m² building, reflecting the absence of services replacement since original construction.
Provision is made for 18 standard WCs and 3 accessible WCs as specified by the client.
aiProse.costNarrative: The works cost reflects full systems replacement in a three-storey building with complex mechanical, electrical and plumbing installations, asbestos removal, and comprehensive strip-out and finishes. Preliminaries are elevated by partial occupation, restricted working hours, term-time constraints, and a hard deadline. Professional fees account for the M&E complexity and BREEAM compliance requirements.
aiProse.roiNarrative: The project cost mid-point is £2,462,000, generating annual energy and operational savings of £95,000, equivalent to a simple payback of 25.9 years. The key financial risk is that actual energy savings may fall short of forecast if building performance in use does not match design assumptions or if utility price inflation diverges from projections.

constraints.title: Vacation-only working
constraints.text: Works must be confined to academic vacation windows, avoiding examination periods in January and May–June, extending the programme and limiting flexibility.

constraints.title: Restricted working hours
constraints.text: Permitted hours are constrained by campus operations, increasing labour costs and potentially extending the construction duration.

constraints.title: Conservation area
constraints.text: External alterations require full planning consent with enhanced materials and detailing, adding cost and approval time.

constraints.title: Asbestos presence
constraints.text: Licensed removal, notification and air testing are required; finds during strip-out can halt work and increase cost.

constraints.title: Ageing M&E services
constraints.text: Existing plant capacity and condition are uncertain; replacement scope may exceed current assumptions, affecting cost and programme.

nextSteps: Commission a refurbishment and demolition asbestos survey immediately to confirm scope, cost and programme impact before Stage 2 design begins.
Obtain pre-application advice from the conservation officer on external alterations, materials and detailing to confirm planning requirements and cost assumptions.
Confirm electrical supply capacity with the utility and commission an M&E condition and capacity survey at Stage 2 to validate the replacement scope.
Agree blackout dates and permitted working hours with the university; build detailed phase plans to fit vacation windows and confirm out-of-hours premium rates.
Prepare a detailed cost plan and risk register at Stage 2, incorporating survey findings and confirming the procurement route and contract form with the client's advisers.

riskRegister.description: Works confined to vacation windows; programme spans multiple academic terms; risk of overrun into term time.
riskRegister.mitigation: Phase works to vacation windows; agree blackout dates with faculty; build programme float; consider out-of-hours working.

riskRegister.description: Restricted working hours extend construction duration and may attract premium or out-of-hours rates.
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm permitted hours with the client; price out-of-hours working where programme-critical; reflect in Prelims.

riskRegister.description: Ageing or inadequate mechanical and electrical services: capacity, condition and compliance of existing plant and distribution are uncertain and may need more replacement than assumed.
riskRegister.mitigation: Commission an M&E condition and capacity survey at Stage 2; confirm supply capacity with the utility early.

riskRegister.description: Asbestos is known or suspected: licensed removal, notification periods and air testing add cost and time, and finds during strip-out can stop work.
riskRegister.mitigation: Commission a refurbishment and demolition asbestos survey before Stage 2 design; carry a provisional sum for removal until it reports.

riskRegister.description: Site is in a conservation area or under an Article 4 direction: external alterations are likely to need full planning, with enhanced materials and detailing.
riskRegister.mitigation: Seek pre-application advice from the conservation officer; assume full planning for external works; allow for enhanced materials when costing.

riskRegister.description: Heating and hot water: electrical capacity and DNO check — raised by the selected scope.
riskRegister.mitigation: Investigate and confirm during Stage 2 design, and carry the outcome into the cost plan.

riskRegister.description: Multiple-phase delivery requires careful sequencing and coordination to avoid disruption to occupied areas and maintain teaching continuity.
riskRegister.mitigation: Confirm phase split and occupation strategy at Stage 2; establish clear handover protocols between phases; maintain liaison with faculty.

riskRegister.description: Design must be completed to tender standard within 32 weeks to meet the 77-week programme and 2028 target date.
riskRegister.mitigation: Establish a robust design programme with clear milestones; allocate resources early; manage scope changes tightly to avoid delays.

aiProse.procurementNarrative: The traditional route with lump-sum pricing and framework direct award suits this project because the design can be completed before tender, cost certainty is a priority, and the client is a public body eligible for framework appointment. The alternative two-stage route would be preferable if early contractor input to sequencing and buildability in this occupied, phased building would justify accepting less price competition at the second stage.
procurementConsiderations: Gaps in the design become client variations under traditional lump-sum delivery; ensure the specification and bills of quantities are complete before tender.
Framework direct award offers less price competition than selective tender; a strong cost consultant should test the appointed contractor's rates against benchmarks.
Public bodies must follow the framework's award rules; confirm that direct appointment is permitted under the selected framework's terms.
procurementConflicts: Traditional lump-sum delivery is slower to site than two-stage; the client's priority to minimise disruption may favour early contractor engagement despite less price certainty.

answers.q3_2_previousWorks: Roof recovered in 2011. Windows replaced on the south elevation in 2016; north elevation original. No services replacement since original construction.
